title: Closed analytical form of many-body free volume and thermodynamics of monodisperse hard disks
authors: Victor M. Pergamenshchik, Taras Bryk, Andrij Trokhymchuk
abstract: The hard disk model is a fundamental reference system for excluded volume physics, liquid structure, and 2D ordering. Yet, despite its apparent simplicity, an analytical formulation of its thermodynamics has remained difficult because the free volume available to disks centers has a highly nontrivial many-body geometry. Here we show that this geometry admits a closed and exact representation: for any given hard disk configuration, the free volume can be analytically expressed through intersection areas of up to five exclusion disks. This provides a direct geometrical route from particle coordinates to the configurational partition function and entropy. We prove that the N disk partition function factorizes into a product of conditional free volumes and identify its two limiting asymptotic forms: the low density fluid regime controlled by extensive cavities and the high density fluid regime controlled by intensive private cells. Using the geometric measures computed from representative equilibrium particle configurations, the resulting theory reproduces the established hard disk equation of state over almost the entire density range up to close packing. At intermediate densities, the analysis reveals a mixed fluid regime in which localized caged defects provide an additional configurational entropy within the density interval preceding liquid hexatic coexistence. Finally, the five disk intersection area is shown to be a sensitive local scalar measure of hexagonal ordering, complementing the orientational order parameter and emphasizing the central role of many-body correlations.
summary: This paper provides a breakthrough analytical theory for the thermodynamics of hard disks by deriving a closed-form expression for the many-body free volume based on geometric intersection areas. It successfully reproduces the known equation of state and reveals complex intermediate fluid regimes. The work establishes a powerful geometric framework for calculating configurational entropy in excluded volume systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the difficulty of analytically formulating the many-body free volume and thermodynamics for the hard disk model due to its complex geometry.
main_result: The authors derive a closed, exact analytical representation for the free volume using intersection areas of up to five exclusion disks, successfully reproducing the equation of state across most density regimes.
method: The methodology involves a rigorous geometric approach to calculate the free volume, leading to factorizations of the partition function based on conditional free volumes.
model_or_system: The system is the monodisperse hard disk model in two dimensions, a fundamental reference system for excluded volume physics and liquid structure.
key_observables: Free volume ($V_{N,n}$), cavity ($\langle C_{N+1} angle_N$), private cell ($c_{N,n}$), and the five-disk intersection area (as an ordering measure).
important_parameters: Density ($\eta$), temperature (implied by equilibrium), and the number of disks ($N$).
main_assumptions: The theory relies on the geometric identity that the free volume can be expressed exactly via intersection areas, and it analyzes limiting regimes (low/high density).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the decomposition of the free volume into the cavity and the private cell within an equilibrium hard disk configuration.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the geometric basis for free volume, deriving exact relationships between free volume, cavity, and private cell, calculating the partition function factorizations, and finally analyzing the equation of state across different fluid regimes.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous derivation of exact geometric measures for configurational entropy and the identification of local order parameters (five-disk intersection area) provide powerful mathematical tools applicable to analyzing complex many-body correlations in quantum systems.

The n-th disk and circle are shown by dashes. The inner white area is the global free volume of the n-th disk, the hatched fraction is its cavity, and the clear fraction is its private cell.

The shown (N −1) disk conﬁguration is allowed as its σ-circles leave a cell (white area) for the N-th disk. However, it is diﬀerent from the equilib- rium conﬁguration of (N −1) disks which is homogeneous. In the equilibrium (N −1) system one of the N −1 disks, whose σ-circle is indicated by solid line, would be at the position shown by dashes.
